notes.meaning: The speaker praises the Lord with his whole being. He declares God's goodness both in small groups of devoted believers and in the large public worship gathering. True praise involves our deepest affections and should be shared with the community of faith.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine taught that giving thanks or confession here means praising God for healing our spiritual wounds, rather than simply confessing sins.

notes.meaning: Everything the Lord has done in creation and in the history of his people is immense and wonderful. Those who love God take deep pleasure in studying and thinking about these great acts. Meditating on what God has done strengthens our faith in him.
All of God's deeds are full of royal majesty and glory. He always acts fairly and remains completely true to his promises. His upright character never changes or fades over time.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine believed that God's most glorious work is justifying ungodly people by giving them his righteousness.

notes.meaning: The Lord performed memorable wonders so his people would never forget his mighty acts. He gave them special memorials and written records to preserve these memories through every generation. Through all of this, he reveals that he is gentle, merciful, and full of kindness.

God provided food and all life necessities for his people who revere him. He took care of Israel in the desert because he promised to keep his sacred covenant with Abraham. Believers can rest assured that God always provides what we need.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Ancient church writers connected the food mentioned here with the Eucharist, seeing it as spiritual nourishment for believers.

notes.meaning: God demonstrated his immense power to his people by driving out hostile nations and giving Israel the land of Canaan. These events proved that their victories came from God's hand rather than human strength. Remembering his power encourages us to rely completely on him.

All the works of God's hands are marked by complete truth and fairness. The laws and commandments he gives are completely dependable and righteous. We can safely build our lives upon his rules because they never mislead us.

God's commandments and promises are firmly established to stand strong forever. Because they are grounded in absolute truth and justice, they will never wear out or change. We can place our full trust in his enduring word through every season.

The Lord brought rescue and freedom to his people when he broke the chains of slavery in Egypt. That rescue pointed forward to the eternal salvation from sin that Christ accomplished. Because God is utterly pure and majestic, his name calls for our deepest awe.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine understood this rescue as our freedom from earthly attachments, drawing believers into the New Covenant rather than seeking worldly wealth.

notes.meaning: True wisdom begins when a person shows loving honor and reverence to the Lord. Those who actually live out his instructions gain deep and practical insight. Honoring God is the highest calling of life and brings praise that will last forever.
